newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambican interior minister and deputy sacked.
newsitem.headline: Mozambican interior minister and deputy sacked.

text.p: Mozambican President Joaquim Chissano has dismissed controversial Interior Minister Manuel Antonio, who came under pressure for the soaring crime rate in the country, Radio Mozambique reported on Friday.
State radio said he would be replaced by Almerinho Manhenje, who will also retain his current post as minister in the presidency for defence and security affairs.
Chissano also sacked Edmundo Carlos Alberto, vice-minister in the Interior Ministry, which controls the police.
The radio did not give reasons for the sackings, but Antonio has been strongly criticised for failing to curb crime and address complaints of ill-treatment of awaiting-trial prisoners.
In an interview with a local newspaper in January he suggested that prisoners only had themselves to blame if they starved to death in police cells.
"They are there because they committed misdeeds and they have to bear the responsibility," he said.
Police figures released this week showed a dramatic increase in crime over the past year, with the number of armed robberies up by nearly 71 percent.
Foreign diplomats have piled the pressure on Chissano's government to take serious measures to curb a wave of violent crime and the failure of the police to catch the culprits.

Diplomats said the government needed to send a strong political signal that it was serious about fighting crime, which would otherwise hamper aid efforts and attempts to rebuild the country's war-shattered economy.
The pressure mounted after the murder of a Swiss anthropologist in September, apparently by robbers, in broad daylight near the capital.

Mozambique is awash with illegal weapons, including assault rifles, left over from a 16-year civil war between rebels and the formerly government that took power on independence from Portugal in 1975.
